findings.title: RULE.DOC.STEER's template sentence leaves a literal unresolved Markdown link in the rendered page
locations: docs/build/guide/rules.html (byte offset ~15226): "the allocating [f](@ref) returns a fresh result" — no wrapper present
policy/docs-rubric.md:70 (source of the quoted sentence): "the allocating [`f`](@ref) returns a"
findings.description: RULE.DOC.STEER's rendered page quotes the in-place steer sentence verbatim, including the placeholder link `[`f`](@ref)`. Because no docstring actually defines a binding named `f`, Documenter's Markdown parser cannot resolve the `@ref` and leaves the raw `[`, `` `f` ``, `]`, `(@ref)` characters as plain rendered text instead of a hyperlink — this is visible only in the built HTML. A reader of the rules page sees a literal, broken-looking `[f](@ref)` in the middle of a sentence. This is an isolated instance (a site-wide sweep of every `](@ref)` occurrence found no other unresolved case), so no class sweep is warranted beyond this one line.
findings.resolution_hint: In policy/docs-rubric.md's RULE.DOC.STEER paragraph, escape the placeholder so CommonMark cannot parse it as a link — e.g. wrap the whole template fragment in a double-backtick code span so it renders as literal text, or spell it without link brackets ("the allocating `f` returns a fresh result instead, `@ref`-linked in the real docstring").
